items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Like our friend Joe Wilder, when he went to take trumpet lessons in Philadelphia the teacher told him his lips was too big.

ctx.x: No, I don’t resent it. I never have been resentment of nobody who’s successful. But I do think they should make an allowance for anybody that’s got the talent whether they’re young or old. ‘Cause I hear some of these youngsters can’t play near as good as some of these old-timers.

In fact a lot of these youngsters are trying to play like the old-timers. No, I think that’s absolutely not fair to any musician to deny him the pleasure of success if he can play regardless of age. Because…J.J. Johnson, he’s not a young man. He signed good contracts, still is. Of course it is controlled by the youngsters.
